summary: Cariboo, BC lookout sharing its name with Mount Alex Graham; burned down in 2017, and a 2021 Facebook post is titled as showing its remains.

facts.status_note: Burned down in 2017; no source describes the site today.

events.note: Facebook group post titled 'Remains of the Alex Graham Fire Lookout, August 2021' (only the title could be read)

evidence.supports: mount located east of Tigulhdzin-chi (Creek), Cariboo Land District
evidence.quote: E of Tigulhdzin-chi (Creek), Cariboo Land District
Labelled Anahim Mountain on BC map 3F, 1921.

evidence.supports: name changed in 1934 to avoid confusion with Anahim Peak
evidence.quote: The name was changed in 1934 to Mount Alex Graham to avoid confusion with Anahim Peak.

evidence.supports: name suggested after Alex Graham, early settler
evidence.quote: Name suggested by Major D.M. MacKay, after Alex Graham, early settler.

evidence.supports: Alex Graham pre-empted land near Alexis Creek and Chilcotin River in 1892
evidence.quote: Mr. Graham pre-empted L 149 near the junction of Alexis Creek and Chilcotin River 21 September 1892

evidence.supports: post titled as showing the remains in August 2021

notes_for_editor: No build date, builder, design, height, staffing or fire cause was found in the two searches and the cached pages, so the story leaves them out. The link between the lookout and Mount Alex Graham is inferred from the shared name; the record's coordinates (52.0822, -122.94985) lie about 40 m from the BC Geographical Names centre point for the mountain (52 deg 04 min 55 sec N, 122 deg 56 min 58 sec W, our calculation), but no source says the lookout stands on the peak. The 'remains' point rests on the title of a Facebook group post; the post body is not readable in the cache. The record's area label reads Cariboo Regional District, which the story does not repeat because Firelookout.ca says only 'Cariboo, BC'; BC Geographical Names uses the Cariboo Land District. No BC Wildfire Service or BC Forest Service record was checked, because the search budget ran out.
